a2-14-wechselpraepositionen.lastLine: ! Jetzt steht es sicher zwischen den Bäumen .
a2-14-wechselpraepositionen.intro: Frieda has a new flat and everyone shows up to help move furniture — which means a whole morning of "put it there / no, it’s already here". The sofa goes against the wall, the lamp between the windows, the boxes into the cellar. Every sentence forces the choice: moving something (wohin? → Akkusativ)
a2-14-wechselpraepositionen.scene: Umzugstag in Friedas neuer Wohnung — Berlin

a2-15-positions-richtungsverben.intro: The class is planning a car-free week for the city, and the office is chaos: plans on the table, maps on the wall, keys stuck in bags, everyone finding a seat. It’s the ideal stage for the position/direction pairs — stellen vs stehen, legen vs liegen, hängen both ways. Meret keeps asking the one que

a2-16-goethe-mini-2.lastLine: Hier bei uns . Wir rufen Sie an .
a2-16-goethe-mini-2.intro: Two weeks before the real exam, the class runs its second big warm-up — and life is providing the material: Timo needs an ID card from the Behörde, has a job interview coming up, and is planning a car-free city day. Every answer recycles a whole phase of grammar. Frau Wolter, behind the counter, jus
a2-16-goethe-mini-2.scene: Aufwärmen vor dem Goethe-Mini-Test 2 — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-17-werden.lastLine: ! Dann sind wir beide auf dem richtigen Weg .
a2-17-werden.intro: A rainy afternoon, a bandaged finger, and a class full of plans for next year — the perfect stage for werden. Neele asks what everyone will do, what they’ll become, and what the weather is turning into, and the little verb does all three jobs at once: future, prediction, change of state.

a2-18-ortsangaben.intro: A tourist stops the class outside the school, lost and looking for the Dom. Everyone jumps in with directions — links, rechts, geradeaus, an der Ampel — and by the time she finds it, the whole class has drilled every location phrase in real conversation.
a2-18-ortsangaben.scene: Vor der Sprachschule — eine Touristin fragt nach dem Weg

a2-19-indirekte-fragen.lastLine: Perfekt ! Dann rufen wir ihn zurück .
a2-19-indirekte-fragen.intro: Between a delayed train, a doctor’s appointment and a mountain of admin, everyone in the group needs information — and nobody wants to sound rude asking for it. Franka shows them the trick: wrap any question in Kannst du mir sagen, …? or Ich weiß nicht, … and it turns polite and indirect, with the v

a2-2-perfekt-review.intro: Monday morning, week two of the A2 course. Everyone comes in full of weekend stories — a flea market, a rented bicycle, a horse — and Insa turns it into the perfect Perfekt workout: haben or sein in position 2, Partizip II at the end. You know every rule already. Today it becomes reflex.

a2-20-was-fuer-ein.lastLine: Klar ! Ich gebe dir ihre Nummer .
a2-20-was-fuer-ein.intro: Solveig is helping at the Bücherei this week — sorting books, running the driving-school desk, and translating for a Gebärdendolmetscher session. Every second conversation starts with was für ein(e): what kind of book, what kind of course, what kind of advice.

a2-21-verben-dativ-akkusativ.lastLine: ürlich ! Ich kaufe dir den Kopfhörer morgen .
a2-21-verben-dativ-akkusativ.intro: It's Karla's birthday, and Timo is showing her the photo album he made — giving her the pictures, explaining the songs, promising the headphones next. Every two-object sentence puts Dativ before Akkusativ: Ich zeige dir das Album, ich schenke dir das Album.

a2-22-konjunktiv2-koennte.lastLine: orgen könnten wir zusammen ein neues kaufen .
a2-22-konjunktiv2-koennte.intro: Ronja is putting together a job application while Timo's cable breaks nearby — and every fix becomes a chance to soften a request: not "Kannst du?" but "Könntest du?", the same offer of help, asked more politely.

a2-23-konjunktiv2-sollte.lastLine: solltest du . Dann bist du nicht im Stress .
a2-23-konjunktiv2-sollte.intro: The Abschlussprüfung is close, and Timo is nervous — so Petra keeps turning bare commands into gentler advice: not "Du sollst mehr üben" but "Du solltest mehr üben", the same idea offered as a recommendation rather than an order.

a2-24-deshalb-trotzdem.lastLine: Danke ! Dann mache ich mir weniger Sorgen .
a2-24-deshalb-trotzdem.intro: A grim forecast splits the class in two: some give in to the rain and stay home, Timo rides anyway. Merle uses the moment to drill the difference — deshalb for the outcome you'd expect, trotzdem for the one that defies it — both triggering inversion.

a2-25-goethe-mini-3.lastLine: Gern ! Viel Erfolg bei der Prüfung !
a2-25-goethe-mini-3.intro: A full afternoon before the final exam: Timo is nervous and looking for advice, and Frau Sander answers with everything from Chapters 19–24 at once — an indirect question, a sollte, a deshalb, a was für ein — all inside one reassuring conversation.

a2-26-adjektiv-bestimmter-artikel.lastLine: ann sind wir bereit für die lange Wanderung .
a2-26-adjektiv-bestimmter-artikel.intro: A shopping trip before a mountain weekend turns into an adjective drill: Ida checks off the warm jacket, the big backpack, the small tent, while Timo makes sure nothing important — the good map — gets left behind. Der/die/das already show gender and case, so almost every adjective just needs -e or -
a2-26-adjektiv-bestimmter-artikel.scene: Einkaufen vor dem Bergwochenende — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-27-adjektiv-unbestimmter-artikel.lastLine: Gute Idee ! Viel Spaß auf dem See !
a2-27-adjektiv-unbestimmter-artikel.intro: A weekend at the national park turns into an adjective drill: Timo needs a small kayak and a warm suit, and Greta hands him a light paddle for a cold day. Unlike der/die/das, ein doesn't always show gender itself — so the adjective has to work harder.
a2-27-adjektiv-unbestimmter-artikel.scene: Ein Ausflug zum Nationalpark — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-28-als-wenn.lastLine: r leid . Aber deine Erinnerungen sind schön .
a2-28-als-wenn.intro: Insa just moved into a new flat with a flatmate, a cat, and a mountain view — the perfect excuse to swap childhood memories (als, her cat Mausi) and daily habits (wenn, whenever her cousin visited with his dog) with Timo. One test decides which word fits: did it happen once, in the past? als. Everyt

a2-29-indefinitpronomen.lastLine: Danke ! Dann ist hier nichts vergessen .
a2-29-indefinitpronomen.intro: Nadja checks in on an empty house while Timo waters the flowers and feeds the waiting cat — and every answer reaches for an indefinite pronoun: niemand is home, nobody has given anything yet, but someone should know where the food is.

a2-3-artikel-review.lastLine: Ja , mach das ! Ich drücke dir die Daumen .
a2-3-artikel-review.intro: Week three, and the language school is buzzing: today there's a small Berufsmesse — a careers fair — in the cafeteria. Merle and Timo wander from table to table meeting a gardener, a bank clerk, a geriatric nurse, weighing whether Merle should switch to something with children. Every job, every plac
a2-3-artikel-review.scene: Berufsmesse in der Cafeteria — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-30-verben-praepositionen.intro: Wibke is waiting for a call in the station hall, dreaming about a career change, while Timo waits with her. Every fixed verb-preposition pair does the talking: warten auf, sich freuen auf, sich interessieren für, glauben an.

a2-31-w-fragen-praepositionen.lastLine: Sie träumt von einer großen Welttournee .
a2-31-w-fragen-praepositionen.intro: A radio interview with a musician gives Alina and Timo plenty to ask about — without ever repeating the noun. Worüber spricht sie? Über ihren Karrierewechsel. Womit hat sie angefangen? Mit einem kleinen Konzert.

a2-32-konjunktiv2-wuensche-hoeflichkeit.intro: A café table becomes a crash course in polite German — Timo would like a bread and a coffee, and Frau Reimers takes his order with hätte, wäre, würde, könnte and sollte, all in one relaxed exchange.

a2-33-relativsatz-nominativ.lastLine: Ich auch . Komm , ich stelle dich vor .
a2-33-relativsatz-nominativ.intro: A radio show about music and culture gives Merit and Timo the perfect excuse to describe people in one flowing sentence: der Mann, der die Nachrichten liest; die Frau, die beim Festival singt; das Kind, das immer tanzt.

a2-34-relativsatz-akkusativ.intro: Wenke is reading a new novel and Timo wants to know everything about it — the author she likes, the chapter she loves most — every description now needing the Akkusativ relative pronoun: der Autor, den ich mag; das Kapitel, das ich liebe.

a2-35-goethe-mini-4.intro: The last afternoon before the real exam: Timo hasn't revised everything, and Silke admits she keeps drifting into the subjunctive — wishing for more time, and looking forward to a stress-free week once it's over. Nothing new — just Chapters 25 through 34, all at once.
a2-35-goethe-mini-4.scene: Der letzte Nachmittag vor der Prüfung — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-4-weil.lastLine: eressant ! Ich finde Sprachen auch spannend .
a2-4-weil.intro: The morning after the careers fair, the classroom is full of questions — and every one of them starts with warum? Kilian explains why he studies so much chemistry (he's training as a medical assistant); Rieke explains why she'd rather learn English and a little Latin. The word weil answers them all,
a2-4-weil.scene: Der Morgen nach der Berufsmesse — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-5-dass.intro: It's film-and-media week, and Marek has started a blog about German films that Frauke isn't sure she trusts. Every "I think…", "I hope…", "I know…" hides the same engine: the word dass, with the verb sliding to the end — just like weil last week.

a2-6-modalverben-praeteritum.lastLine: omantisch ! Du hast wirklich etwas verpasst .
a2-6-modalverben-praeteritum.intro: A quiet Monday, and Anke wants to know why Timo missed the wedding — work, his boss said no — swapping stories about what everyone could, had to, and wanted to do. The modal past — konnte, musste, wollte — is how Germans actually narrate it.
a2-6-modalverben-praeteritum.scene: Montagmorgen — Geschichten vom Wochenende, Sprachschule Berlin

a2-7-possessivartikel-dativ.intro: Silke checks in on her dog, and Nils reports back — how he's doing, whether he barks at the neighbour, whether he's playing with his ball. Every story about someone and their animal needs a dative possessive: mit meinem Hund, bei ihren Eltern.
a2-7-possessivartikel-dativ.scene: Haustiergeschichten vor dem Kursfest — Sprachschule Berlin

a2-8-komparativ-superlativ.lastLine: kt ! Das ist die beste Entscheidung für ihn .
a2-8-komparativ-superlativ.intro: Sina and Timo argue over which school suits their son better — bigger, with a shorter walk, or the one with the best gym — and every argument reaches for a comparison: größer als, am schönsten, der beste.

a2-9-vergleiche-als-wie.intro: Film night is being planned, and Jara and Timo can't agree — is this trailer better than the last one, or just as exciting? The evening becomes a live drill in als for a difference and wie for an equality.

b1-1-infinitiv-mit-zu.intro: Renke is planning to spend the summer camping and lazing around outdoors, and Timo wants to know why — every plan expressed with zu + Infinitiv: Ich plane, zu campen. Ich habe vor, mich zu entspannen.

b1-10-passiv-praesens.lastLine: n Problem ! Danach werden die Haare geföhnt .
b1-10-passiv-praesens.intro: At the hairdresser's, Timo asks what's being done to his hair today, and Frau Bruns answers step by step — washed, then cut, coloured only on request. The present passive puts the process front and centre, not who's doing it.
b1-10-passiv-praesens.scene: Ein Besuch im Museum und beim Friseur

b1-11-relativsaetze-dativ.intro: A stormy forecast has Marret and Timo comparing who they trust — the weather forecast, the dark clouds, the storm neither of them quite believes — every description built on a Dativ relative clause: der Mann, dem ich vertraue; die Prognose, der ich glaube.

b1-12-adjektivdeklination-wiederholung.lastLine: Ah ja . Das ist eine wichtige Voraussetzung .
b1-12-adjektivdeklination-wiederholung.intro: Antje has written a new job application — cover letter, CV, a photo Timo calls compelling — and every document needs one more certificate, one more adjective ending, weak, mixed or strong, all doing the same job: showing gender, number and case exactly once.
b1-12-adjektivdeklination-wiederholung.scene: Ein Café am Nachmittag — Antje zeigt Timo ihre Bewerbung

b1-13-goethe-mini-2.lastLine: Perfekt ! Ich rufe ihn gleich an .
b1-13-goethe-mini-2.intro: Timo and Grit spend a Saturday running errands — an apartment viewing with high extra costs, an excited decision to call the landlord today — recycling obwohl, wegen, and a polite Konjunktiv II offer all at once.

b1-14-komparativ-superlativ-vor-nomen.intro: Wiebke and Timo compare neighbourhoods — a bigger park here, a better traffic situation there, the highest quality of life somewhere else — every comparison landing directly in front of a noun, with the declension ending riding along: der schnellere Weg, das größte Grün.
b1-14-komparativ-superlativ-vor-nomen.scene: Im Café — Wiebke und Timo vergleichen Wohnungen und Städte

b1-15-n-deklination.intro: Silje and Timo run through the people they know — a lawyer, a judge, a chemist, maybe a reporter — every one of them an N-Deklination noun that quietly grows an -n or -en in every case but the first.

b1-16-futur1.lastLine: Klar ! Das wird bestimmt gut funktionieren .
b1-16-futur1.intro: On Silvesterabend, Emke and Timo plan their year ahead — a smart home, blinds and lights controlled from a phone, a budget kept modest — using Futur I for plans, predictions, promises and assumptions about what's coming.
b1-16-futur1.scene: Silvesterabend — Emke und Timo planen das neue Jahr

b1-17-nebensatz-damit-um-zu.lastLine: weniger Plastik , um die Umwelt zu schützen .
b1-17-nebensatz-damit-um-zu.intro: Antke returns bottles for the deposit while Timo sorts the trash so the environment gets cleaner — every action justified with a purpose clause, some with um…zu, some with damit, depending on who's doing what.
b1-17-nebensatz-damit-um-zu.scene: Samstagvormittag — Antke und Timo sortieren den Müll

b1-18-relativsaetze-mit-praepositionen.intro: A walk through the city gives Marlen and Timo landmarks, monuments, and narrow alleys to describe — every one needing a relative clause where the preposition stays glued to the pronoun: der Turm, mit dem wir beginnen; die Gasse, in der wir stehen.

b1-19-goethe-halbzeit-test.lastLine: Danke ! Das macht mir einen guten Eindruck .
b1-19-goethe-halbzeit-test.intro: A long Saturday: Uta wants to apply for an apartment fast because the price is good, and Timo — despite his nerves — offers her honest feedback on the application letter, recycling everything from the first half of B1 in one continuous story.
b1-19-goethe-halbzeit-test.scene: Ein langer Samstag in der Stadt

b1-2-nebensaetze-weil-da-obwohl.lastLine: l ich lieber im Auto bleibe , komme ich mit .
b1-2-nebensaetze-weil-da-obwohl.intro: Frauke has lost her appetite for camping — it's too cold outside — while Timo wants to go to the beach anyway. Every reason and every unexpected contrast reaches for weil, da, or obwohl, all sending the verb to the very end.

b1-20-plusquamperfekt.intro: Wenke and Timo catch up on old friends they lost touch with — she had already moved before they stopped seeing each other, he had finished his studies before he moved away too — every memory built on two layers of the past: what had already happened, and what came next.

b1-21-temporale-nebensaetze.lastLine: rüber sprechen , fühle ich mich erleichtert .
b1-21-temporale-nebensaetze.intro: Runa and Timo work through a small disagreement about noise and headphones — since she moved in, before he speaks, while she sleeps — using all five ways German answers "when?": als, wenn, bevor, nachdem, während.

b1-22-brauchen-zu-infinitiv.intro: Katrin sets up online banking while Timo reassures her it's easier than she thinks — she doesn't need to visit the bank, doesn't need to check her balance daily. müssen says what you have to do; brauchen nicht … zu says what you don't.

b1-23-reflexivpronomen-akkusativ-dativ.lastLine: underbar ! Du erholst dich wirklich schnell .
b1-23-reflexivpronomen-akkusativ-dativ.intro: Timo is recovering in hospital after a small accident, and Frauke helps him through his morning routine — brushing his teeth, getting his medication, feeding himself — every reflexive verb revealing whether it needs mich/dich or mir/dir.

b1-24-zweiteilige-konnektoren.intro: Nike and Timo compare music tastes and plan a concert trip — she likes both jazz and metal, he likes neither; she listens to not only music but also podcasts — every opinion built on a two-part connector.

b1-25-stellung-von-nicht.lastLine: ch bin froh , dass wir nicht gezögert haben .
b1-25-stellung-von-nicht.intro: Sinje and Timo pass an honesty-box newspaper stand — she won't take the change, because that isn't right, and won't keep the wallet either — a small moral test of exactly what "nicht" is negating each time.

b1-26-adjektiv-ohne-artikel.lastLine: Dann wird das ein zeitloses Stück .
b1-26-adjektiv-ohne-artikel.intro: Yara needs talented actors and colourful costumes for the school play, and Timo offers musical friends from choir and old costumes from home — every noun phrase here has no article at all, so the adjective alone must carry gender, case and number.

b1-27-goethe-mini-3.intro: Marte and Timo compare a demanding week — a job interview that exhausted her, a delayed connection, a doctor's visit — recycling Plusquamperfekt, temporal clauses, and two-part connectors from every B1 chapter so far.

b1-28-passiv-praesens-praeteritum-perfek.lastLine: e sind durch Infomaterial informiert worden .
b1-28-passiv-praesens-praeteritum-perfek.intro: At an environmental-action fair, Insa and Timo read reports on recycling improvements, planted trees, and monitored drinking water — the same action phrased in three tenses: wird verbessert, wurde verbessert, ist verbessert worden.

b1-29-passiv-modalverben.lastLine: Das klingt vernünftig . Ich stimme zu .
b1-29-passiv-modalverben.intro: A lecture on the European Union has Solveig and Timo working through contracts that must be signed, decisions that must be made, member states that must be informed — the passive combined with every modal verb, werden always last.
